articles.title: MP aponta R$ 4 milhões a empresa ligada a ex-secretário preso em Bauru | G1
articles.standfirst: Documentos da Operação Cavalo de Troia detalham transações feitas à empresa Core, que seria usada como intermediária para repassar vantagens indevidas a Renato Purini. Um dos pagamentos, de R$ 750 mil, foi feito no dia em que a Câmara votou o projeto que autorizava a concessão do serviço de esgoto.
articles.summary: A Operação Cavalo de Troia detalha repasses de R$ 4 milhões a Renato Purini, com pagamentos realizados durante votações cruciais na Câmara de Bauru.
articles.body:
Novos documentos do Ministério Público detalham pagamentos feitos pela Estre Ambiental à empresa Core, que, segundo a investigação da Operação Cavalo de Troia , teria ligação com Renato Purini, ex-secretário de Governo de Bauru (SP) e marido da prefeita Suéllen Rosim .

Purini está preso e é investigado no caso que apura suspeitas de fraude na licitação para a concessão de serviços relacionados à gestão de resíduos sólidos no município.

De acordo com o MP, os pagamentos à Core somam quase R$ 4 milhões e teriam sido realizados por meio de notas fiscais relacionadas a diferentes contratos de consultoria. Para os investigadores, as transações indicariam um fluxo financeiro contínuo e estruturado, e não repasses isolados à empresa.

Os documentos apontam pagamentos entre 8 de dezembro de 2025 e 27 de agosto de 2026. Também há uma nota emitida em 8 de setembro, mas os investigadores não localizaram a baixa desse documento.

Novos trechos do documento do MP que embasa as investigações da Operação Cavalo de Troia — Foto: TV TEM/ Reprodução

No dia 23 de outubro, na terceira fase da operação, foram cumpridos mandados de busca e apreensão em São Paulo e houve a prisão de Jonathan Moga Pinto, diretor da Core. ( Veja abaixo mais detalhes sobre essa fase da operação) .

Nessa fase, o Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco) informou que o objetivo foi atingir o braço financeiro da suposta organização criada para fraudar a licitação.

Tabela disponibilizada no documento do Ministério Público mostra pagamentos à empresa que teriam ligação com Purini — Foto: TV TEM/ Reprodução

Um dos pagamentos destacados pelo Ministério Público foi realizado em 8 de setembro, no valor de R$ 750 mil. Na mesma data, a Câmara Municipal de Bauru votou o projeto de lei que autorizava a concessão do serviço de esgoto que, por enquanto, não é o alvo da investigação.

Segundo o MP, mensagens analisadas na investigação indicariam que, naquele dia, Purini manteve intensa articulação política para assegurar a aprovação do projeto.

A investigação apura suspeitas de que a Core teria sido utilizada como intermediária para que o ex-secretário recebesse vantagens indevidas. As conclusões apresentadas nos documentos fazem parte das investigações que ainda estão em curso.

Renato Purini foi preso em 16 de outubro e está na Penitenciária II de Potim, no Vale do Paraíba. A reportagem entrou em contato com a defesa do ex-secretário, mas não obteve resposta até a publicação.

Empresa de fachada para repasses de propina

Jonathan Moga Pinto é preso na terceira fase da Operação Cavalo de Troia deflagrado pelo Gaeco — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

A partir da localização de um documento fiscal, o Ministério Público aprofundou as diligências sobre a empresa para identificar a origem e o destino do dinheiro

“Essa frente investigativa foi aprofundada após a apreensão, na fase anterior da Operação Cavalo de Troia, de uma nota fiscal emitida pela empresa que estaria intermediando as propinas. As diligências realizadas posteriormente identificaram outros pagamentos expressivos em favor da mesma empresa”, informou o MPSP em nota.

De acordo com o Ministério Público, a Core foi criada em agosto de 2025 por Kauê Tadeu Daher Crudeli com capital reduzido e sem nenhum funcionário registrado. Inicialmente cadastrada para consultoria em gestão empresarial, a firma posteriormente adicionou serviços de seguros, previdência e saúde.

A promotoria apontou ainda que a empresa e seu fundador mantinham vínculos diretos com o advogado Marcos Libanore Caldeira, apontado como intermediário dos repasses feitos pela concessionária Estre Ambiental a Renato Purini.

“A constituição recente da empresa, o reduzido capital social, a ausência de funcionários e a falta de correspondência aparente entre as atividades dos responsáveis e o serviço descrito no documento fiscal são elementos suspeitos que reforçam a incompatibilidade entre o serviço contratado e a empresa”, justificou o órgão.

Gaeco realiza operação para cumprir mandados de busca e apreensão em secretarias de Bauru — Foto: Luís Negrelli

Segundo as investigações, Jonathan Moga Pinto assumiu a direção da empresa em dezembro de 2025, período que coincide com reuniões estratégicas entre os envolvidos no esquema. Documentos mostram que ele assinou como titular da firma em 19 de dezembro, mesma data em que a Estre Ambiental efetuou repasses de R$ 750 mil e R$ 225 mil para a Core.

Os valores suspeitos identificados pela investigação superam R$ 4 milhões, por meio de contratos e notas fiscais cuja prestação de serviço jamais foi comprovada. Para o MP, a estrutura empresarial foi montada para a "simulação de contratações e emissão de notas fiscais representativas de serviços não prestados".

A Justiça determinou o bloqueio de bens e ativos financeiros no valor de R$ 20 milhões dos quatro investigados: Renato Purini, Marcos Libanore Caldeira, Jonathan Moga Pinto e Kauê Tadeu Daher Crudeli. As ações da operação contaram com o apoio da Polícia Militar.

A apuração aponta que os agentes públicos e representantes de empresas privadas teriam atuado em conjunto para direcionar uma licitação estimada em mais de R$ 5,2 bilhões, com duração prevista de 30 anos.

A primeira fase da operação foi realizada em 9 de setembro de 2026. Em 16 de outubro, uma nova etapa levou à prisão do então secretário municipal de Governo, Renato Purini, marido da prefeita Suéllen Rosim (PSD).

O Ministério Público apresentou denúncia contra seis investigados na primeira etapa, que se tornaram réus no processo , e a investigação avançou com a análise de materiais apreendidos, mensagens e indícios da participação de outros agentes públicos e particulares.

O Ministério Público investigava possíveis irregularidades envolvendo a Associação dos Catadores de Reciclagem de Bauru (Ascam), que mantinha contratos com a prefeitura para serviços relacionados à coleta seletiva.

Segundo as investigações, Valdomiro Pereira da Silva Filho, empresário e marido da então presidente da associação, Gisele Moretti, teria utilizado sua influência para intimidar trabalhadores.

A análise de conversas e ligações do casal levou os investigadores a identificar indícios de outras irregularidades, incluindo possíveis pedidos de propina e interferências na futura concessão dos serviços de gestão de resíduos sólidos.

As apurações deram origem a duas frentes de investigação: a Operação Mobius, relacionada a possíveis irregularidades em contratos de coleta seletiva, e a Operação Cavalo de Troia, voltada à suspeita de direcionamento da concessão do lixo.

O nome Cavalo de Troia faz referência à principal suspeita investigada: a possível inserção de pessoas com vínculos com a empresa Estre Ambiental em posições estratégicas da administração municipal para influenciar decisões relacionadas à contratação pública.

Associação dos Catadores de Materiais Recicláveis (Ascam) em Bauru (SP) — Foto: Divulgação

O foco principal é a suspeita de que um grupo formado por agentes públicos, executivos e funcionários de empresas privadas, consultores e intermediários tenha atuado para favorecer a empresa na licitação da concessão dos serviços de gestão de resíduos sólidos urbanos.

O projeto previa um contrato de 30 anos, com valor estimado em mais de R$ 5,2 bilhões, considerado o maior contrato público projetado na história de Bauru.

De acordo com o Ministério Público, o suposto esquema não teria começado com a publicação do edital. A investigação aponta que as irregularidades teriam sido articuladas ainda na fase de preparação do projeto, com possíveis interferências nos estudos técnicos, na modelagem econômica, nos critérios de habilitação e julgamento e na elaboração de documentos administrativos.

Os investigadores também apuram suspeitas de pagamentos de vantagens indevidas, compartilhamento reservado de informações, pressão sobre servidores públicos e tentativas de interferir na atuação de órgãos de controle.

A denúncia apresentada pelo MP atribui aos seis já denunciados crimes como organização criminosa, contratação direta ilegal e fraude ao caráter competitivo de licitação . Também descreve episódios específicos de corrupção ativa e passiva envolvendo parte dos acusados. O envolvimento de outras pessoas ainda é investigado.

Gaeco aponta relação entre ex-secretária Cilene Bordezan e CEO Hamilton Libório Agle — Foto: Reprodução

Ex-secretária municipal de Meio Ambiente de Bauru, Cilene é uma das principais investigadas. Segundo o Ministério Público, ela teria atuado na estruturação da concessão dentro da prefeitura em alinhamento com interesses da empresa Estre Ambiental.

A investigação aponta que ela mantinha contato frequente com Hamilton Libório Agle, executivo da empresa, e que os dois teriam discutido aspectos da concessão antes da publicação do edital.

Conversas extraídas de celulares e outros elementos reunidos pelos investigadores são apontados pelo MP como indícios de que Cilene teria participado de articulações relacionadas à modelagem do projeto e à condução de procedimentos administrativos.

Ela foi presa na primeira fase da operação e exonerada do cargo.

Executivo da Estre Ambiental, Hamilton é apontado pelo Ministério Público como um dos articuladores do suposto esquema.

Segundo a investigação, ele teria atuado para influenciar a preparação da concessão e obter vantagens para a empresa, inclusive por meio de contatos com agentes públicos e da discussão de aspectos técnicos e econômicos do projeto.

Mensagens e outros elementos apreendidos são citados pelo MP como indícios de alinhamento entre ele e a então secretária de Meio Ambiente. Hamilton está preso desde o início da ação em setembro.

Marido da prefeita de Bauru e secretário, Renato Purini foi preso durante operação do Gaeco — Foto: TV TEM

Marido da prefeita Suéllen Rosim e então secretário municipal de Governo, Renato Purini foi preso em 16 de outubro, durante a segunda fase da Operação Cavalo de Troia.

A nova etapa foi realizada após a análise de materiais apreendidos anteriormente, que, segundo o Ministério Público, revelou indícios da participação de outros agentes públicos e particulares nas práticas investigadas.

De acordo com o MP, Purini teria atuado como uma figura política do grupo investigado, com participação em articulações relacionadas à concessão. A investigação também apura possíveis repasses ilícitos a agentes públicos e vereadores.

A Justiça negou um pedido de habeas corpus apresentado pela defesa e manteve a prisão preventiva do ex-secretário. Após a prisão, Suéllen Rosim exonerou o marido do cargo. A prefeita não é apontada como alvo da operação criminal nas informações divulgadas sobre essa fase.

Também estão entre os denunciados pelo Ministério Público:

Vitor João de Freitas Costa: ex-secretário municipal dos Negócios Jurídicos;

Sara Moura de Jesus: ex-secretária-adjunta de Meio Ambiente;

Talita de Andrade Soares Chieregatti: funcionária da Estre Ambiental;

Mário Luiz Silvério: coordenador técnico ligado à Fundação Instituto de Pesquisas Econômicas (Fipe).

Talita de Andrade Soares Chieregatti foi transferida para prisão domiciliar após pedido da defesa aceito pela Justiça no dia 8 de outubro e Mario Luiz Silvério é considerado foragido. Os demais seguem presos.

A primeira fase também atingiu Gisele Moretti, então presidente da Ascam, e Valdomiro Pereira da Silva Filho, empresário e marido dela, no contexto das investigações relacionadas à coleta seletiva.

Os dois foram detidos temporariamente na deflagração das ações e liberados após o fim do prazo da prisão temporária para cumprir medidas cautelares. As responsabilidades individuais de cada um ainda precisam ser estabelecidas pela Justiça.

Renato Purini chega à Central de Polícia Judiciária (CPJ) após operação do Gaeco, nesta sexta-feira (16), em Bauru (SP) — Foto: Luís Negrelli/TV TEM

Suspeita de direcionamento de uma concessão bilionária: Segundo o Ministério Público, o grupo teria atuado para criar condições que favorecessem uma empresa na disputa pela concessão dos serviços de gestão de resíduos sólidos. A investigação aponta que a possível fraude teria envolvido diferentes etapas, desde a elaboração dos estudos técnicos até a definição de critérios e exigências do edital. O objetivo, segundo a acusação, seria restringir a concorrência e aumentar as chances de vitória da empresa favorecida.

Relação entre a ex-secretária e executivo: Mensagens encontradas pelos investigadores indicariam uma relação próxima entre Cilene Bordezan e Hamilton Agle, além de conversas sobre o andamento da concessão. Para o Ministério Público, os diálogos são indícios de que interesses privados teriam influenciado decisões e procedimentos que deveriam ser conduzidos pela administração pública.

Possível atuação de um grupo organizado: A denúncia apresentada pelo MP descreve uma estrutura com divisão de tarefas entre agentes públicos e particulares. Segundo a acusação, os envolvidos teriam atuado de maneira coordenada para influenciar a preparação da concessão, compartilhar informações reservadas e interferir em procedimentos administrativos. O Ministério Público também aponta suspeitas de pagamentos de vantagens indevidas e tentativas de contornar mecanismos de fiscalização.

Dinheiro apreendido e análise de documentos: Na primeira fase, os investigadores apreenderam R$ 240 mil em dinheiro na residência do então secretário municipal dos Negócios Jurídicos, Vitor João de Freitas Costa. O valor foi citado na investigação no contexto das suspeitas de vantagens econômicas indevidas. Além do dinheiro, celulares, documentos e outros materiais apreendidos passaram a integrar as apurações. A análise desse conteúdo contribuiu para o avanço do caso e para a realização da segunda fase da operação, em outubro.

Denúncia contra seis investigados: Em setembro, o Ministério Público apresentou à Justiça uma denúncia criminal contra seis pessoas investigadas na primeira fase. O documento, com 317 páginas, descreve a suposta atuação de uma organização criminosa e atribui aos denunciados crimes relacionados à fraude em contratação pública e à corrupção. O recebimento da denúncia pela Justiça e o andamento do processo são etapas distintas da investigação policial e da acusação apresentada pelo Ministério Público.

Gaeco aponta que ex-secretária de Bauru articulou concessão do lixo em grupo do WhatsApp antes de assumir cargo — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

A concessão, que previa a gestão dos resíduos sólidos de Bauru por 30 anos, foi estimada em mais de R$ 5,2 bilhões.

O procedimento foi suspenso pelo Tribunal de Contas do Estado de São Paulo (TCE-SP), após questionamentos relacionados ao edital. A suspensão impediu o avanço da concorrência nos moldes inicialmente previstos, mas não encerrou as investigações criminais.

O Ministério Público apura justamente se o processo foi estruturado para favorecer uma empresa e se houve interferência indevida na preparação do projeto e na condução dos procedimentos administrativos.

Em manifestação após a prisão do então CEO da empresa, a Estre Ambiental informou que está colaborando integralmente com as investigações, prestando todos os esclarecimentos, e confirmou que não vai participar da licitação do lixo em Bauru. A empresa afirmou ainda que está adotando as providências necessárias para se desvincular do processo.

Renato Purini prestou depoimento na quinta-feira (22) ao Ministério Público após ter sido transferido do CDP de Bauru para Penitenciária de Potim. O ex-secretário e marido da prefeita optou por permanecer em silêncio durante depoimento.

Purini foi interrogado por videoconferência diretamente da penitenciária, que fica no Vale do Paraíba, onde está preso de forma preventiva. ( Veja no vídeo abaixo ).

Já a prefeitura de Bauru, na nota divulgada após a segunda fase da operação, que prendeu o então secretário de governo Renato Purini, marido da prefeita Suéllen Rosim, disse que "desde o início das investigações conduzidas pelo Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (GAECO), tem colaborado integralmente com as autoridades, fornecendo documentos, informações e os esclarecimentos solicitados, e seguirá contribuindo com tudo o que for necessário para o avanço das apurações."

A prefeita não é alvo da operação do Gaeco até o momento, mas é investigada em uma Comissão Processante aberta na Câmara dos Vereadores que apura negligência dela na elaboração do edital da licitação do lixo.

Suéllen Rosim foi ouvida na CP no dia 16 de outubro , horas depois da prisão do marido. Durante o depoimento, Suéllen afirmou que o marido não participava das decisões sobre o edital do lixo, negou ter recebido vantagens indevidas e disse desconhecer encontros entre ele e o executivo da Estre Ambiental, empresa apontada como possível beneficiária do direcionamento da licitação.

Em nota, a prefeita informou que adotou todas as medidas administrativas necessárias, pautando suas decisões pela responsabilidade, transparência e imparcialidade. Ela afirmou ainda que confia no esclarecimento dos fatos em momento oportuno e que seguirá cumprindo suas funções à frente do município.

O g1 não conseguiu contato com as defesas dos demais investigados presos na operação.

O ex-secretário de Governo Renato Purini, marido da prefeita de Bauru (SP), Suéllen Rosim (PSD), foi preso na manhã desta sexta-feira (16) durante operação deflagrada pelo Gaeco — Foto: Redes Sociais/Reprodução

articles.title: Moradores bloqueiam RJ-116 em protesto por falta d’água | G1
articles.standfirst: Manifestantes queimaram pneus em Papucaia para cobrar uma solução da Águas do Rio e da prefeitura; concessionária atribui problema às chuvas.
articles.summary: Manifestantes queimaram pneus em Papucaia para cobrar uma solução da Águas do Rio e da prefeitura; concessionária atribui problema às chuvas.
articles.body:
Moradores de Cachoeiras de Macacu , na Região Serrana do Rio, realizaram um protesto na noite desta segunda-feira (26) por causa da falta de água no município. A manifestação aconteceu na RJ-116, na altura do bairro Papucaia, onde os participantes queimaram pneus e interditaram parcialmente a via.

Segundo os moradores, o abastecimento está parado há três dias. Durante o protesto, eles cobraram um posicionamento da concessionária Águas do Rio e da Prefeitura de Cachoeiras de Macacu e pediram a normalização do fornecimento de água.

A concessionária Águas do Rio informou que as unidades de tratamento Posto Pena e Rio Souza tiveram as operações impactadas pelas fortes chuvas que atingiram a região. Ainda de acordo com a concessionária, o abastecimento emergencial está sendo realizado por meio de caminhões-pipa, com prioridade para unidades de saúde e instituições de ensino.

Moradores de Cachoeiras de Macacu protestaram na rodovia contra a falta de água. — Foto: Redes Sociais

A Águas do Rio também destacou que, apesar de ter pago integralmente a outorga de R$ 58 milhões à Prefeitura de Cachoeiras de Macacu, afirma que ainda não conseguiu exercer plenamente o contrato de concessão. Segundo a empresa, isso ocorre devido ao descumprimento de obrigações contratuais por parte do município.

Em razão do impasse, foram abertos processos junto à Agência Reguladora de Energia e Saneamento Básico do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Agenersa) e também no Poder Judiciário. A concessionária informou que busca, por meio dessas medidas, garantir o cumprimento das condições previstas no contrato de concessão.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Cachoeiras de Macacu contestou as declarações da concessionária Águas do Rio e afirmou que a alegação de descumprimento contratual por parte do município "não procede". Segundo a administração municipal, a justificativa seria uma forma de desviar o foco dos problemas estruturais das unidades operadas pela empresa.

De acordo com a prefeitura, a causa da crise no abastecimento é técnica e está ligada à falta de investimentos nas unidades desde o início da concessão, em 2021. O município destaca que os transtornos afetam inclusive moradores que já eram atendidos pela antiga Cedae, sem qualquer relação com a autarquia municipal.

A administração também informou que, além das ações envolvendo a prefeitura, existem processos movidos por associações comerciais e de moradores contra a concessionária.

A Prefeitura de Cachoeiras de Macacu cobrou o cumprimento das obrigações da Águas do Rio e a normalização do abastecimento. Em nota, reforçou que a água é um bem essencial e que a falta do serviço tem provocado impactos significativos na rotina da população.

articles.title: Vídeo mostra duas onças-pardas caminhando por condomínio em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Vídeos feitos por morador em Novo Horizonte registram os felinos circulando tranquilamente pelo terreno, enquanto galinhas-d’angola seguem os animais; especialista explica o comportamento da espécie e os cuidados necessários para evitar conflitos.
articles.summary: Vídeos feitos por morador em Novo Horizonte registram os felinos circulando tranquilamente pelo terreno, enquanto galinhas-d’angola seguem os animais.
articles.body:
Duas onças-pardas caminhando tranquilamente por um terreno e um grupo de galinhas-d’angola seguindo os felinos. A cena, registrada em vídeo pelo morador Ercole José Bononi, chamou a atenção em um condomínio de chácaras em Novo Horizonte (SP), no interior paulista.

Em uma das gravações, as duas onças aparecem próximas ao muro do imóvel , enquanto as aves caminham logo atrás. A movimentação chega a dar a impressão de que as galinhas estão tentando 'expulsar' os visitantes da área.

Apesar da cena curiosa, o flagrante também chama a atenção para a convivência entre a fauna silvestre e as áreas ocupadas pelo ser humano, que avançam sobre ambientes naturais.

Segundo Ercole, os animais vistos nas imagens são jovens. Ele acredita que sejam filhotes de uma fêmea que também circulou pelo local, mas a identificação dos indivíduos e o possível parentesco entre eles não foram confirmados.

“Esses dois que apareceram beirando o muro já são mais sossegados. Acho que são filhotões. A mãe é grandona e muito mais arisca, se abaixa quando percebe alguma coisa”, conta o morador.

Duas onças são flagradas em condomínio — Foto: Ercole José Bononi

Onças podem aparecer sozinhas ou acompanhadas dos filhotes

Para Yara Barros, bióloga e pesquisadora do Projeto Onças do Iguaçu, as imagens mostram dois indivíduos de onça-parda, mas não permitem afirmar se são mãe e filhote ou dois filhotes.

A especialista explica que as onças-pardas têm hábitos solitários. Por isso, a presença de dois animais juntos não significa necessariamente que formem um casal.

“Onças não andam em casais. Isso acontece apenas durante o cio da fêmea, que pode durar de seis a 16 dias”, explica Yara.

No caso registrado em Novo Horizonte, a hipótese de que os animais sejam mãe e filhote é uma possibilidade levantada pelo morador, mas que precisa ser confirmada.

Morador relata ataques a galinhas-d’angola

Morador começou a perceber a presença das onças depois de encontrar galinhas-d’angola atacadas — Foto: Ercole José Bononi

Ercole conta que começou a perceber a presença das onças depois de encontrar galinhas-d’angola atacadas durante a madrugada. Ao todo, segundo ele, nove aves foram mortas pelos felinos .

O morador relata que os ataques aconteciam principalmente entre três e quatro horas da manhã. A gravação das duas onças próximas ao muro, no entanto, foi feita por volta das quatro horas da tarde, horário que o surpreendeu.

“Eu só sei que tem as onças aqui devido às angolas, que fazem aquele 'tropé'. Senão, a gente não ia saber que tem a onça”, relata.

Ele também afirma ter acompanhado os pontos por onde os animais entravam no condomínio e reforçado uma abertura na tela de alambrado que separa a área de uma mata próxima. Depois do reparo, deixou de avistar as onças do lado de dentro do condomínio, embora acredite que elas continuem circulando nas redondezas.

Além das galinhas, Ercole menciona outros animais silvestres na região, como capivaras, bugios, antas, tamanduás-bandeira e lobos-guarás. Ele também relata ter observado um pônei atacado nas proximidades, em uma propriedade vizinha. Esses episódios, porém, não foram confirmados de forma independente.

Avanço sobre áreas naturais aumenta encontros com a fauna

A presença de animais silvestres perto de casas, chácaras e condomínios precisa ser entendida também a partir das transformações nos ambientes naturais.

A expansão das áreas ocupadas pelo ser humano, o desmatamento e a fragmentação dos habitats reduzem e alteram os espaços utilizados pela fauna, aumentando as possibilidades de encontros com as pessoas.

Em regiões próximas a fragmentos de mata, a presença de animais domésticos também pode favorecer conflitos. Galinhas mantidas em espaços desprotegidos, por exemplo, podem se tornar presas acessíveis para predadores silvestres.

Yara explica que, quando as onças estão na borda da mata e as aves não contam com proteção adequada, como galinheiros reforçados, ataques a galinhas podem acontecer.

Por isso, a recomendação é investir em estruturas que mantenham os animais domésticos protegidos, especialmente durante a noite, e evitar que a presença de presas fáceis atraia os felinos para perto das residências.

Onças-pardas não devem ser perseguidas ou acuadas

Apesar do porte e da força, as onças-pardas geralmente evitam o contato com seres humanos . Quando respeitadas e mantidas a uma distância segura, não costumam representar perigo às pessoas. Ainda assim, são animais silvestres e podem reagir de forma defensiva se forem acuados, perseguidos ou surpreendidos de perto.

Ao encontrar um felino, a orientação é manter distância, não tentar se aproximar para fotografar ou filmar, não oferecer alimento e não bloquear a rota de fuga do animal.

Em situações como a registrada em Novo Horizonte, é importante comunicar os responsáveis pela conservação da fauna, como o Centro Nacional de Pesquisa e Conservação de Mamíferos Carnívoros (CENAP), do Instituto Chico Mendes de Conservação da Biodiversidade (ICMBio), que pode orientar sobre a ocorrência e as medidas adequadas para prevenir conflitos entre a fauna silvestre e os moradores.

articles.summary: KOTA: Around 40 students of Govt Tribal Girls Ashram Hostel at Pachhad in Baran district have written to SP Abhishek Andasu alleging molestation, repeated
articles.body: KOTA: Around 40 students of Govt Tribal Girls Ashram Hostel at Pachhad in Baran district have written to SP Abhishek Andasu alleging molestation, repeated harassment and verbal abuse by the husband of a sports coach, who they claim makes frequent unauthorized visits to the hostel premises.The students, all of them minors, along with hostel superintendent Mamta Gautam, formally approached the SP Sunday, seeking urgent intervention and legal action against the accused, identified as Premshankar Meena, husband of coach Ramsarekha Bai.According to complaints submitted separately by students and the hostel superintendent, copies of which are with TOI, Meena routinely enters the hostel, often in an inebriated state, before proceeding to molest, harass and verbally abuse minor students.An already distressing situation escalated last Saturday night, when Meena allegedly scaled the hostel's boundary wall and entered the premises unlawfully around 8pm. Once inside, he molested several girls and used foul language, the complaints state.The students claimed this last incident in particular affected the hostel's atmosphere.Hostel authorities said they tried to report Saturday’s incident to Chhipabarod police station immediately, but no action was initiated.Fearing for their safety and frustrated by the lack of response from police, the students and hostel superintendent decided to approach the Baran SP directly, demanding legal action against Meena and steps to restore a secure environment at the hostel.Some of the complainants also shared a video they claimed documents their allegations and added that Meena’s actions have created fear among them.Baran SP Andasu, ASP Sourabh Tiwari, Chhipabarod area DSP Tarachand and circle inspector Gambhir Singh did not respond to repeated calls seeking their responses to the matter.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. articles.title: 'Apologise to nation': Rijiju targets Congress after Army debunks Chinese intrusion claims
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday hit out at the Congress for circulating an AI-generated video falsely attributing claims about Chinese
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday hit out at the Congress for circulating an AI-generated video falsely attributing claims about Chinese control of areas in Arunachal Pradesh to an Indian Army officer, escalating the political face-off over the clip.Leading the BJP's counterattack, Union minister Kiren Rijiju accused the Congress of sharing the fabricated video featuring Lieutenant General Girish Kalia and demanded an apology for allegedly tarnishing the Army's image.In a post on X, Rijiju demanded an apology from the opposition party, writing, "Congress Party must apologize to the nation for spreading fake AI video to tarnish the image of Indian Army.""This is a treacherous act and is on par with the vile deeds of our enemies. The Congress Party is running a despicable campaign on behalf of India's enemies," the Union minister added.The row erupted after Congress shared a post on Monday alleging that China had captured the three areas in Arunachal Pradesh.Congress leader Ritu Choudhary on X wrote: "Shameful! Lieutenant General Girish Kalia (GOC, Spear Corps) says that China has captured Asafila, Longju, and Taksing circles in Arunachal Pradesh. Despite demands for logistics (supplies), there are reports that the army is being deployed against 'Gen Z' instead of China," Choudhary wrote.The Indian Army's fact-check unit also debunked the viral video, saying it had been digitally altered and contained fabricated remarks attributed to the officer.In a post on X, the Army said: "A digitally altered video is being circulated with fabricated remarks attributed to Lt Gen Girish Kalia, claiming that China has taken control of Asaphila, Longjou and Taksing Circle in Arunachal Pradesh and that the Indian Army has been denied essential supplies. The misleading video attempts to portray fabricated statements as a leaked admission by a senior Indian Army officer. The video uses Synthetic Generated Information to falsely attribute remarks to Lt Gen Girish Kalia. The original footage relates to a press briefing delivered by then GOC 28 Infantry Division, Maj Gen Girish Kalia, in Kupwara, Jammu & Kashmir, on 27 October 2023. He addressed infiltration attempts across the Line of Control, reporting 10 foiled attempts, the elimination of 27 terrorists and the recovery of warlike stores and narcotics. He made no such statements about Chinese control over Arunachal Pradesh or denial of supplies to the Indian Army..."The Army clarified that the original footage was from a press briefing held in Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir, on October 27, 2023, when then Major General Girish Kalia spoke about infiltration attempts across the Line of Control. According to the Army, he reported 10 foiled infiltration attempts, the elimination of 27 terrorists and the recovery of weapons and narcotics.The Army said the officer had made no statements about Chinese control over areas in Arunachal Pradesh or the denial of supplies to Indian troops.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Delhi high court declines to halt probe against woman journalist accused of casteist remarks against ACP at Jantar Mantar, seeks police response
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Tuesday refused to stay the investigation into a case registered against a woman journalist over alleged casteist
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Tuesday refused to stay the investigation into a case registered against a woman journalist over alleged casteist remarks and public humiliation of a police officer during a protest near Jantar Mantar earlier this month.Justice Mini Pushkarna clarified that the court was neither rejecting the interim prayer at this stage nor passing any order on it, news agency PTI reported.The court issued notice to the Delhi Police and the assistant commissioner of police (ACP), who filed the complaint, on the journalist’s plea seeking quashing of the FIR. It asked them to file their replies before November 16, the next date of hearing.“I am not rejecting any prayer as of now. I am only issuing notice to them. The matter needs consideration; list for final hearing on November 16,” the judge said.Earlier, the woman journalist had filed a sexual assault complaint against the official. The Delhi Police Crime Branch is investigating her complaint, PTI reported.The journalist’s counsel argued that the FIR lodged by the ACP was intended to intimidate her and prevent her from pursuing the complaint against him.The high court passed a similar order on a separate plea by a male colleague of the journalist, who has also sought quashing of the FIR registered against him.The Delhi Police registered the FIR against the independent journalist and others based on an official’s complaint, PTI reported.The officer, who is posted at the Connaught Place sub-division of New Delhi district, alleged that casteist remarks, public humiliation and defamation were directed at him during the protest.The FIR invokes relevant provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Sections 221 (obstructing a public servant from discharging duty), 356(2) (defamation) and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: A Nevada couple is donating $150 million to build the state’s first stand-alone children’s hospital; decades ago, a hospital saved their child’s life
articles.summary: Three decades ago, Felicia Horowitz watched her child receive lifesaving treatment at Lucile Packard Children’s Hospital Stanford in California.
articles.body: Three decades ago, Felicia Horowitz watched her child receive lifesaving treatment at Lucile Packard Children’s Hospital Stanford in California. During that difficult period, she noticed the Packard name displayed on the hospital walls and made a personal promise to herself that if she and her husband, Ben Horowitz, could one day afford to do so, they would give back to help other families facing similar circumstances. That promise has now taken shape in a major philanthropic commitment. The couple has pledged $150 million towards Nevada’s first stand-alone children’s hospital, a project intended to expand access to specialised paediatric healthcare in a state where families have long faced challenges obtaining complex treatment close to home.A decades-old promise becomes a major philanthropic commitmentThe donation was announced on October 23, 2026, by Intermountain Foundation. The new facility will be named the Intermountain Health Felicia and Ben Horowitz Children’s Hospital in recognition of the couple’s contribution. According to Intermountain Health, the gift is among the largest publicly announced donations to a children’s hospital in the United States.Felicia Horowitz is president of the Horowitz Family Foundation and co-founder and president of The Paid in Full Foundation. Her husband, Ben Horowitz, is a co-founder and general partner of the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, also known as a16z.The contribution forms part of the Nevada Campaign for Kids, a wider philanthropic effort supporting the hospital’s development. For the couple, the project offers an opportunity to turn a deeply personal experience into support for families who may otherwise struggle to access specialised medical services.Why Nevada needs a stand-alone children’s hospitalSouthern Nevada has long lacked a dedicated, comprehensive children’s hospital capable of bringing a broad range of specialised paediatric services together under one roof. According to the Las Vegas Sun, Las Vegas is the largest metropolitan area in the United States without a stand-alone children’s hospital. The publication also reported that Nevada ranks 48th in paediatricians per capita and that nearly 30,000 Nevada families leave the state annually to seek healthcare for their children.For families requiring complex procedures or specialist consultations, travelling out of state can mean additional expenses, time away from work and the difficulty of managing a child’s treatment far from home. A dedicated facility in Las Vegas is intended to reduce those barriers by expanding local access to specialist teams and advanced paediatric services.Ben Horowitz said he was surprised to discover the gap in children’s healthcare after moving to Southern Nevada with his wife about five years ago. He expressed the hope that families would no longer have to face the risk of losing a child because the necessary medical expertise was unavailable locally.Inside the $1 billion hospital projectThe hospital is being developed at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas’ Harry Reid Research and Technology Park in southwest Las Vegas. The overall project is estimated to cost more than $1 billion, making it a major healthcare infrastructure investment for the region.The planned facility will cover approximately 828,600 square feet across a 33-acre campus. Its inpatient tower is expected to open in 2030 with 180 beds, with space to expand capacity to 228 beds as demand grows.Intermountain Health has committed to funding a substantial share of the project, while donations from individuals and organisations are helping support the campaign. The Horowitz family’s $150 million pledge represents a major contribution towards the development and its broader ambition to improve children’s healthcare in Nevada.The project broke ground on October 26, 2026. Once operational, the hospital is expected to create around 1,300 jobs and generate an estimated $800 million in annual economic impact for Clark County, according to the Las Vegas Sun.Specialised care, research and medical talentBeyond its inpatient facilities, the hospital is intended to strengthen the region’s ability to provide specialised treatment for children. Intermountain Health says the investment will help recruit experienced paediatric healthcare professionals, develop specialised programmes and advance medical research.Behavioural health is among the areas the health system has identified as a priority, alongside broader access to specialist paediatric care. Recruiting physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals will be central to establishing the hospital’s services and building expertise within Nevada.The project is also connected to Intermountain Health’s wider paediatric healthcare network. The organisation operates Primary Children’s Hospitals in Utah and is expanding paediatric services in Billings, Montana. Its stated ambition is to connect specialist knowledge, research and treatment across the communities it serves, allowing developments in one location to benefit children elsewhere in the network.Other major donors are backing the hospitalThe Horowitz family’s pledge follows several other substantial contributions to the Nevada Campaign for Kids. According to the Las Vegas Sun, Larry and Heidi Canarelli pledged $50 million earlier in October. In August, the Las Vegas Raiders and three of the franchise’s co-owners committed a combined $25 million. Singer Bruno Mars also contributed $1 million at a public event in April.Felicia Horowitz has emphasised that improving children’s health requires contributions from across the community. She hopes families will regard the future hospital as a shared institution, built to serve children throughout Nevada rather than as a project belonging to any one donor.You use AI every day. articles.title: For 25 years, Andy Willis helped people in Banburyshire through hardship; the dyslexic campaigner has now won a national award for his work supporting vulnerable families
articles.summary: Andy Willis, a community campaigner who has spent 25 years volunteering and supporting people through difficult circumstances, has won a national award
articles.body: Andy Willis, a community campaigner who has spent 25 years volunteering and supporting people through difficult circumstances, has won a national award recognising his contribution to vulnerable individuals and families in Banburyshire, England. Willis was named the winner of the Community Shining Star Award (20+) at the Dyslexia Awards 2026, held in Telford on October 17, according to the official awards website and local newspaper Banbury Guardian.Known locally as the “People’s Champion”, Willis was recognised for his work as founder, patron and Head of Information, Advice and Wellbeing at Banburyshire Advice Centre. His voluntary work spans 25 years, including around two decades dedicated specifically to advice services that help people understand and access the support available to them.“I am absolutely thrilled and deeply humbled to receive this award,” Willis told Banbury Guardian. He said the recognition reflected the work of the advice centre and the resilience of the local community. “Being dyslexic has never stopped me from wanting to make a difference and I hope this inspires others to see that neurodiversity is a strength,” he added.The Community Shining Star Award, sponsored by Bespoke Computing Ltd, recognises adults aged 20 and above whose work has made a meaningful difference in their communities. The Dyslexia Awards, founded in 2015 by Elizabeth Wilkinson MBE, aim to celebrate the abilities, achievements and contributions of dyslexic people while challenging misconceptions about the condition.Helping people navigate the benefits systemWillis’s work focuses on a problem that can be difficult for people already facing financial or personal hardship: understanding which support they qualify for and navigating the forms and procedures required to access it. Banburyshire Advice Centre is an independent charity that provides guidance on benefits and general advice. Its volunteers help people complete benefit applications, while the centre can also issue foodbank vouchers to those in need. Its services include career guidance and tax advice for older people.The centre serves communities across Oxfordshire, Northamptonshire, Warwickshire and Buckinghamshire. Its work is particularly relevant to residents who may struggle to navigate complex systems or identify the assistance available to them. The organisation is run by the registered charity Banburyshire Citizen Project, which was established in 2016. According to the project’s account of its origins, Willis recognised a need for a dedicated advice service as local provision changed and deprivation affected parts of Banbury.The charity says it has also produced reports on social deprivation for Parliament and raised issues affecting its clients with local and national decision-makers.From court service to community supportWillis’s route into advice work began after he worked in the County Court Service as a court usher and administrator. He later moved into education, teaching children, teenagers and adults, where he encountered the difficulties families faced when dealing with food insecurity and bereavement. Those experiences helped lead him towards advice work, which he has been involved in since 2006, according to the charity’s website.He subsequently volunteered with organisations including the Banbury Benefits Advice Project and Age UK Oxfordshire. At Age UK, he spent nearly a decade helping older people deal with practical and emotional challenges involving finances, welfare and heating.His wider voluntary work has included supporting the MS Society, Contact the Elderly and the Workers’ Educational Association. He also campaigned on issues involving mental health, disability and older people for organisations including Mind, Leonard Cheshire and the Alzheimer’s Society.In recognition of his community work, Willis received the British Citizen Award at the Palace of Westminster in January 2019. The Open University also awarded him an honorary Master’s degree in 2019 for his services to society and charity. In 2020, he received the UK government’s Points of Light award, which recognises outstanding individual volunteers.The government’s award profile said Willis had raised more than £60,000 to establish the Banburyshire Citizen Project and more than £20,000 for the Workers’ Educational Association. It also highlighted the advice centre’s telephone support during the Covid-19 pandemic, when residents needed guidance on issues including furlough, redundancy and benefits.In 2022, Willis was named Supporter of the Year by mental health charity Rethink Mental Illness for his campaigning and work helping people with mental health difficulties access disability benefits.Challenging stereotypes about dyslexiaThe latest award also puts the spotlight on Willis’s message that dyslexia should not be seen only in terms of the challenges it can create. He has spoken about wanting other dyslexic and neurodivergent people to recognise their abilities and pursue their ambitions.The Dyslexia Awards describe their mission as celebrating the skills and achievements of dyslexic people across fields including the arts, entrepreneurship, innovation, science and community service. Their Community Shining Star category recognises people whose contributions have had a positive impact beyond their own professional or personal lives.For Willis, the recognition comes after years of work supporting residents through financial pressures, disability-related challenges and other difficult circumstances. The award also acknowledges the contribution of the volunteers and colleagues who help deliver the advice centre’s services.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: UK and EU officials to discuss freedom of movement
articles.summary: Officials are expected to begin discussions on a range of options for the future UK-EU relationship before a summit next month.
articles.body:
British and European officials will discuss the future options for the UK's relationship with the EU, Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds has told the BBC.

Officials on both sides are expected to begin discussions about a range of options, including free movement, before the EU summit on 20 November.

However, Downing Street has insisted the government's current focus is on achieving new deals in areas such as food and youth mobility at the summit.

Reynolds said no "assumptions" had been made about what the UK's future relationship with Brussels could look like.

Andy Burnham has said he wants an "honest discussion" about the prospect of returning to free movement between the UK and EU.

But the prime minister has been clear any major changes to the UK-EU relationship would require a mandate at a general election, which is due by 2029.

He has vowed to stick by the red lines in Labour's 2024 manifesto, with no return to freedom of movement, the EU single market or customs union, for the duration of this parliamentary session, which will end by 2029.

Freedom of movement, which allows EU citizens to travel, live, study and work in any member country, is a precondition of membership of the EU's single market.

The single market enables goods, services and people to move freely between member states, with countries also applying many common rules and standards.

No 10 appears to backtrack on PM's freedom of movement referendum suggestion

Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

Burnham open to 'honest discussion' on EU free movement

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Reynolds said current discussions ahead of the summit are around food and drink, electricity and emissions trading.

He said: "What the prime minister has also said, quite rightly, is we face a series of policy changes on the European side that will affect us.

"We need to get as little uncertainty as possible, we need to have a way to resolve what our long-term relationship will be and he is going to set that out after the summit.

"He is going to be frank with the British people about what the trade-offs are but no assumptions have been made on that."

Pressed on whether UK officials are talking to the EU about freedom of movement Reynolds said: "They will be talking to them about what the future options for our relationship might be.

"But here and now, the focus should be on the summit and the tangible difference improvements we're going to make."

A government spokesperson stressed there were no current discussions on freedom of movement.

"We are working with the EU on the areas set out and agreed ahead of the UK-EU Summit and within the manifesto red lines," the spokesperson added.

Burnham is far more willing to have a public conversation around Brexit than his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer, whose government was nervous about reopening a debate that proved so contentious in the past.

Some people within the Labour Party had been urging Sir Keir to go further and there is a widely held view that Burnham's comments are likely to go down well with voters tempted by the Liberal Democrats and Greens.

But there is nervousness among Labour MPs with small majorities in Brexit-supporting, Reform-facing constituencies.

Labour MP Melanie Onn, whose constituency Great Grimsby and Cleethorpes backed leaving the EU, told the Today programme Burnham risked losing trust by talking about going beyond the 2024 manifesto at a future election.

"I don't think that the scars have healed for many people around the country so I do think this is an unnecessary conversation to be having at this time," she said.

Onn, who lost her seat in 2019 to the Conservatives but won it back in 2024, warned against re-opening the conversation, saying: "Trust is incredibly important, it's hard-earned and easily lost, and on this matter I think that we should tread incredibly carefully."

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage told BBC Breakfast that "Andy Burnham has no mandate to be in Brussels, to be negotiating any of this" and called for the prime minister to put his ideas to the public in a general election.

On Monday, Burnham left the door open to a potential referendum on freedom of movement with the EU.

The prime minister caused some confusion when he told broadcasters that he would not reintroduce free movement without a referendum, but Downing Street later said no decisions had been made on whether a public vote would be needed.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told the BBC on Sunday that no options for the UK's future relationship could be taken off the table.

But Burnham did appear to draw some red lines of his own when he told the Sunday Times that he would not be in favour of the UK joining the euro or the border-free Schengen zone.

The fact the prime minister has not been willing to say the same thing about free movement is being seen in Westminster as evidence that he believes it is a genuine option.

articles.title: After directing Schindler’s List in 1993, Steven Spielberg donated his share of the film’s profits to a foundation; the organisation has since distributed more than $160 million in grants
articles.summary: When Steven Spielberg directed Schindler’s List in 1993, the experience left a lasting impact on him, inspiring a philanthropic commitment that has
articles.body: When Steven Spielberg directed Schindler’s List in 1993, the experience left a lasting impact on him, inspiring a philanthropic commitment that has continued for decades. The filmmaker donated his share of the film’s profits to establish the Righteous Persons Foundation in 1994, with the aim of strengthening Jewish life, preserving historical memory and supporting initiatives that promote social justice. Since its establishment, the foundation has expanded its work beyond Holocaust education to include arts, culture, documentary filmmaking and efforts to build understanding between communities. According to its official website, the organisation has distributed more than $160 million in grants, supporting projects that preserve Jewish heritage, amplify overlooked stories and encourage a more inclusive society.How Schindler’s List inspired the foundationReleased in 1993, Schindler’s List tells the story of German industrialist Oskar Schindler, who saved more than 1,000 Jews during the Holocaust by employing them in his factories. The film, based on Thomas Keneally’s novel Schindler’s Ark, brought the history of the Holocaust to a global audience and became one of Spielberg’s most acclaimed works.Spielberg’s experience directing the film motivated him to establish the Righteous Persons Foundation the following year. In August 1994, the Jewish Telegraphic Agency reported that all his personal profits from the film would go towards the newly established organisation. The foundation began operating in the autumn of 1994, with its initial priorities including Holocaust education and support for Jewish causes in the United States. The foundation’s vision was not limited to preserving the past. It also sought to strengthen contemporary Jewish communities by supporting education, cultural initiatives and social justice efforts.A philanthropic effort that grew beyond one filmThe foundation’s work expanded as Spielberg and his wife, actress Kate Capshaw, contributed additional funds. Spielberg also designated profits from his films Munich (2005) and Lincoln (2012) for the organisation, according to its official website.In 2005, profits from Munich, which explores the aftermath of the 1972 Munich Olympics massacre, helped establish the foundation’s Media Fund for Co-existence. An initial $5 million allocation supported projects using media and storytelling to encourage understanding between people from different backgrounds.Among the initiatives supported through the fund were Arab Labor, a television sitcom about the life of an Arab Israeli journalist, and Israel Story, a radio programme and podcast exploring Israeli society. The projects reflected the foundation’s belief that storytelling can help audiences understand experiences beyond their own.More than $160 million distributed in grantsThe Righteous Persons Foundation reports that it has distributed more than $160 million in grants since its establishment. Its funding has supported organisations working in Jewish history, education, arts and culture, documentary filmmaking, social justice and intercultural understanding.The grants have backed both established institutions and projects seeking new ways to engage audiences with history and contemporary social issues. The foundation has also supported efforts to make Jewish cultural traditions accessible to younger generations and to encourage dialogue across religious and cultural divides.Its grantmaking has evolved over time, but its central aim remains to strengthen Jewish life while promoting dignity, justice and a deeper understanding of different communities. The $160 million figure represents the foundation’s cumulative grantmaking as reported on its own website.Preserving Holocaust survivors’ testimoniesOne of the foundation’s significant areas of support has been the preservation of Holocaust survivor testimony through the USC Shoah Foundation, an independent institute established by Spielberg in 1994.The institute records and preserves the experiences of Holocaust survivors and other witnesses of genocide, making their accounts available for education and research. The Righteous Persons Foundation provided substantial support towards establishing the organisation and has continued to fund its work.In 2024, the foundation pledged $30 million over six years to the USC Shoah Foundation’s endowment. According to the grant announcement, the funding is intended to help preserve testimonies, provide opportunities for additional survivors and liberators to record their experiences, and strengthen the institute’s educational programmes.The grant reflects a long-term commitment to ensuring that survivor accounts remain accessible to future generations, particularly as the number of living Holocaust survivors declines. The two organisations remain independent, with the USC Shoah Foundation focused on testimony and education and the Righteous Persons Foundation operating as a grantmaking organisation.Supporting documentary films and Jewish cultureThe foundation has also invested in documentary filmmaking as a way to explore Jewish identity, history and social issues. In 1996, it helped establish a documentary film fund at the Foundation for Jewish Culture.The fund supported projects including Trembling Before G-d, which examines the experiences of gay and lesbian Orthodox Jews, and Waltz with Bashir, an animated documentary about memory and the Lebanon War. The foundation says the initiative backed close to 100 documentaries.Another major cultural project involved the digitisation of Yiddish literature. In 1998, the foundation became the lead funder of the Yiddish Book Center’s effort to preserve and make Yiddish books available online. The resulting Steven Spielberg Digital Yiddish Library contains digitised copies of more than 11,000 distinct titles, according to the foundation.Subsequent support helped fund translators working to make Yiddish literature available in English, widening access to a literary tradition that might otherwise be difficult for new generations to explore.Helping Holocaust survivors access reparationsThe foundation’s work has also included practical assistance for Holocaust survivors. In 2008, it supported Bet Tzedek, a legal services organisation, in establishing the Holocaust Survivor Justice Network.The network brought together attorneys who volunteered to help survivors navigate the process of seeking reparations from the German government. According to the foundation’s account, the network had helped more than 5,000 survivors obtain an estimated $25 million in reparations by the time of its published update.The initiative demonstrated how grantmaking could help survivors access compensation through legal assistance, particularly when complex procedures created barriers. It also extended the foundation’s work beyond historical preservation and education to address the needs of people who lived through the Holocaust.A lasting commitment to history and communityThe Righteous Persons Foundation’s work has developed into a broad philanthropic programme connecting cultural preservation, education, storytelling and social justice. Its grants have supported Holocaust testimony, documentary films, Jewish literature and projects that encourage dialogue between communities.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: New Rs 1,000 note with temple design? PIB Fact Check debunks viral claim
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Press Information Bureau’s (PIB) Fact Check unit on Tuesday debunked claims about a new Rs 1,000 currency note.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Press Information Bureau’s (PIB) Fact Check unit on Tuesday debunked claims about a new Rs 1,000 currency note. The clarification came after images and videos of a purported yellow-coloured note featuring a temple motif went viral on social media, with some posts claiming it had been issued or would enter circulation on the 15th.PIB Fact Check clarified that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has made no announcement regarding the issuance of a new Rs 1,000 banknote.In a post on X, PIB Fact Check said, “Several social media posts claim that a new Rs 1,000 note has been issued. This claim is fake.”The agency added, “The @RBI has made no announcement regarding the issuance of a new Rs 1,000 note.” It also urged people to “Verify information through official sources and do not share unverified claims.”The clarification came after the purported note appeared in posts shared across platforms including Instagram, X and Telegram.The Rs 1,000 denomination was withdrawn from circulation during the demonetisation announced on November 8, 2016, when the government withdrew the legal tender status of the old Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes.New Rs 500 notes were subsequently introduced, while the RBI brought in Rs 2,000 notes as the highest-denomination banknotes in the new currency series. In May 2023, the RBI announced the withdrawal of Rs 2,000 notes from circulation, while clarifying that they would continue to be legal tender.Banknotes in denominations of Rs 10, Rs 20, Rs 50, Rs 100, Rs 200 and Rs 500 remain in circulation under the RBI’s Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series.PIB Fact Check has urged people to verify currency-related announcements through official sources and avoid forwarding unverified claims.The viral posts should not be treated as confirmation of a new denomination unless the RBI issues an official announcement.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A British collector spent four decades gathering Admiral Lord Horatio Nelson’s letters, naval documents and manuscripts​;​ the archive, including letters to Emma Hamilton, is now up for auction at Sotheby’s for an estimated £4 million to £6 million
articles.summary: Rare letters and documents belonging to Navy commander Vice-Admiral Lord Horatio Nelson are up for auction at Sotheby’s as part of a collection of 415
articles.body: Rare letters and documents belonging to Navy commander Vice-Admiral Lord Horatio Nelson are up for auction at Sotheby’s as part of a collection of 415 historical documents, manuscripts and letters. The lot also includes notes Nelson wrote to his lover, Emma Hamilton. Sotheby’s expects the auction to fetch between £4 million and £6 million. The auction house opened bidding on Wednesday, the anniversary of the Battle of Trafalgar, and bidding runs until 18 November.Clive Richards, CBE (1937–2021), a venture capitalist and philanthropist with strong roots in Herefordshire, collected these rare letters and manuscripts. All proceeds from the auction will go to the Clive Richards Foundation, which supports education, healthcare, heritage and the arts, the auction house said.A rare collection built over four decadesThe lot contains 415 documents, manuscripts and letters. The historic collection comprises the Nelson Papers (217 items), Hamilton Papers (136 items), Battle Papers (46 items) and Nelson Family Papers (19 items), according to Sotheby’s. It took Richards more than 40 years to gather these rare letters.Gabriel Heaton, Sotheby’s book and manuscript specialist, told the Press Association that while the auction house often sells individual letters by Nelson or Emma Hamilton, selling an entire collection of this size is far rarer. This is “the greatest collection of its kind in private hands”, she said.“We’re really privileged to be presenting here the Clive Richards collection of letters and documents relating to Admiral Nelson, one of the towering figures of British history. What we have here is a wonderful collection of hundreds of letters covering every aspect of Nelson’s life and career, and of those closest to him, and those who served alongside him,” Heaton said.“Nelson is such a widely loved and respected figure. There are so many aspects to him that it’s pretty hard to pin him down to just one personal location.”Nelson PapersThe core of the archive is the Nelson Papers, which include 168 letters written by Nelson himself. The documents cover major moments of the Napoleonic Wars, including Bastia, Cape St Vincent, the Nile, Copenhagen and Trafalgar. Some letters were written after he lost the sight of one eye. Others were written after his right arm was amputated and show him learning to write with his left hand. The collection also holds Nelson’s handwritten reports on the battles of the Nile and Copenhagen, along with his battle plans for Trafalgar.Letters to Emma HamiltonThe lot includes 24 letters to Hamilton, which offer a rare glimpse into their relationship. They were married to other people when the affair began, but they were unapologetic about it. In one letter dated January 1800 and written at sea, Nelson describes a dream he had about Hamilton: “Last night I did nothing but dream of you.” In the letter, he recounted how she embraced him and whispered, “I love nothing but you, my Nelson.” He also wrote about kissing her “fervently” afterwards. “We enjoy’d the height of love,” he wrote.The sale also includes the Nelson Family Papers, which trace the wider history of his relatives through letters exchanged between them. Dominic Sandbrook, co-host of the podcast The Rest Is History, says the collection is rich and exciting for anyone interested in Nelson, the Royal Navy or the Napoleonic Wars.“For anybody interested in Nelson, the Royal Navy, the Napoleonic Wars or British history generally, this is an extraordinarily rich and exciting collection. Indeed, some of these letters and documents, such as Nelson’s handwritten reports on the battles of the Nile and Copenhagen, or his battle plans for Trafalgar, rank alongside the most sacred texts of our national history,” Sandbrook said.“Stirring and touching by turns, these are truly wonderful things. If only I had made better decisions when I was young and gone into AI development instead of writing history books, I would be throwing every last penny at this myself.”Nelson died at the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805, aged 47. Monuments across Britain honour him, the best known being Nelson’s Column in Trafalgar Square. When the bidding closes next month, the lucky buyer will own the papers of a man who spent much of his life at sea, writing letters when he was not fighting.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Canadian woodworker began cutting trees for an off-grid cabin and spent years harvesting and milling logs through harsh winters; after building up a stockpile of 300 logs, he finished his handmade woodland retreat
articles.summary: The dream of living in the wilderness often starts with the promise of simplicity, but building a home far from modern conveniences requires patience,
articles.body: The dream of living in the wilderness often starts with the promise of simplicity, but building a home far from modern conveniences requires patience, resilience and a willingness to work with nature on its own terms. For Canadian woodworker Cody Bokshowan, that dream became a reality, one tree at a time, with years of hard work in freezing conditions. What started as an ambitious timber-collecting expedition ended up as a fully functional log cabin, handcrafted from trees he felled and lumber he milled himself.A dream that grew in the forestOnline, Bokshowan is known as Trustin Timber, and documents woodworking, self-reliance and wilderness life. One of his videos shows the long process behind his off-grid cabin, a project that began eight years ago with the painstaking task of cutting down trees for its construction, as reported by Diario AS S.L.He decided to do the work himself instead of buying ready-made timber, from felling trees in the forest to preparing the logs for building. This method required a lot of physical effort, especially during the winter months when temperatures dropped and conditions worsened.The cold was a challenge before the work even started. The sap would not flow in the winter chill, so Bokshowan often had to start cutting trees in freezing weather, before the exertion of the task could warm him up. He was learning the trade when he first began, but he gradually acquired the skills needed to cope with the demanding work.5 logs to 300Media reported that the project’s scope became clearer over the years. Bokshowan’s timber collection was built up slowly, beginning with just five logs, then 10, then 100 and then a fantastic collection of 300 logs.The growing collection was more than just raw material. It was years of experience, better technique and better understanding of working in the forest.Media reports said that Bokshowan gradually became more skilled in controlling the direction that trees fell, learning how to guide trees to specific landing spots without using ropes, pulleys or levers. He also learned how to dress for the harsh climate, which made long hours outside more bearable.Building a retreat out of the landYears of logging and timber milling finally came together to create a handmade woodland retreat. The cabin is constructed from trees in the surrounding forest and demonstrates a labor intensive way of building where materials and structure are closely connected to the landscape.For Bokshowan, the finished cabin is the culmination of an eight-year labor of love that proves how grit and a few handy skills can turn a remote wilderness dream into a solid home. His project also demonstrates the patience required to build an off-grid lifestyle, where even the most basic building material can take years of labor before becoming part of a finished structure.Images Courtesy: Instagram/trustintimberYou use AI every day. articles.title: 'Can’t take a chance': Trump campaigns for Cindy Hyde-Smith amid Republican midterm worries
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has vowed to overcome the historical trend of the ruling party losing ground in midterm elections, using a rally in Mississippi
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has vowed to overcome the historical trend of the ruling party losing ground in midterm elections, using a rally in Mississippi to campaign for Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith ahead of the November 3 polls.Addressing supporters in Corinth on Monday, Trump claimed his rallies had changed the political conversation around the midterms, expressing confidence that Republicans could defy expectations despite concerns over voter enthusiasm and the cost of living.“For some reason, presidents don’t do well in the midterm, no matter how good they are, even if they’re great, like us,” Trump said, adding that no president had campaigned as extensively for midterm elections as he had.According to CNN, Trump acknowledged that he could not afford to take Hyde-Smith’s Senate seat for granted, despite Mississippi being a traditionally Republican state.“I’m here because Cindy’s doing great, but I just got to make sure. I can’t take a chance,” Trump said.Trump touts economic record, downplays cost-of-living concernsDuring the rally, Trump portrayed the US economy as thriving, repeatedly describing the country as experiencing a “golden age” of prosperity. However, he made little mention of inflation and rising gasoline prices, which have added to concerns over household expenses.Trump defended his administration’s handling of the war with Iran, claiming that the US had inflicted a major defeat on the Islamic Republic and arguing that the resulting increase in gas prices would be temporary.He also pointed to stock market gains as evidence that his economic policies were working, urging voters to consider their retirement savings before casting their ballots.“Your 401ks are 60% higher,” Trump said while making his case for Hyde-Smith. He encouraged supporters who were uncertain about voting for the senator to check their retirement accounts.The president's remarks came as Republicans face concerns about enthusiasm among their supporters, while Democrats seek to capitalise on opposition to Trump's policies ahead of the midterm elections.Trump speaks with strained voice, responds to Obama criticismTrump's campaign schedule across Republican-leaning states appeared to take a toll on his voice during the Mississippi appearance. He joked about the strain of holding rallies almost daily, saying God had not made vocal cords for such an intense schedule.The president also discussed his renovation work at the White House, a subject that has drawn criticism from former president Barack Obama.Responding to Obama's remarks about his focus on renovations, Trump said the former president did not understand the importance of maintaining the building.“The White House has to be clean, pristine, beautiful,” Trump said, defending the work.Trump's speech at the Crossroads Arena in Corinth drew a sizeable crowd, although CNN reported that large sections of the venue had emptied by the time he was wrapping up.The rally formed part of Trump's broader effort to help Republicans retain their congressional seats as the November 3 midterm elections approach. Historically, the president's party tends to lose seats in Congress during midterm elections, making the contests a key test of the administration's political standing.You use AI every day. articles.title: Is Jagan Reddy's 'regret' message a calculated alliance pitch for Congress?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Is YSRCP supremo YS Jagan Mohan Reddy signalling a drift towards the Congress-led INDIA bloc?
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Is YSRCP supremo YS Jagan Mohan Reddy signalling a drift towards the Congress-led INDIA bloc? Or is he trying to break free from the image of being soft on the BJP?The former Andhra Pradesh chief minister has provided issue-based support to the BJP-led NDA government on several key legislations in Parliament while he was in power in the state. However, he has stayed away from joining any alliance till now. So, when Jagan Reddy recently regretted his “mistake” of supporting the 2023 NDA legislation for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner, it fuelled speculation about his future political moves."We regret supporting the process under which the ruling party nominates the Chief Election Commissioner at the Centre. Neither the CEC nor the SEC should be appointed by the ruling party. The selection committee should comprise the Prime Minister, the leader of the opposition and the Chief Justice of India (CJI), with all three exercising their voting rights," the YSRCP chief said recently, calling the current selection system "flawed."The timing and context of Jagan’s remarks are significant. So, is he rethinking his “solo” politics? And if yes, will the Congress be ready to tango with him in Andhra Pradesh? After all, alliances with regional parties have been the Congress’s biggest Achilles heel across states.Jagan’s support for NDA’s key BillsJagan Mohan Reddy’s MPs backed the Modi government several times between 2019 and 2024, both in Lok Sabha and in Rajya Sabha, on many important legislations. However, when it came to stitching an alliance for the 2024 elections, the BJP ignored Jagan’s help and joined hands with his arch-rival Chandrababu Naidu. Together, TDP and BJP swept the polls in Andhra Pradesh, winning 164 out of 175 seats in the assembly and 21 out of 25 seats in Lok Sabha. The YSRCP was reduced to 11 seats in the assembly and 4 in Lok Sabha.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Despite being spurned by the BJP and his party’s shock defeat, Jagan Mohan Reddy remained confident about his BJP ties. Jagan even announced that his MPs would extend issue-based support to the NDA government in matters concerning national and state interest.But with the BJP heavily dependent on Chandrababu Naidu’s support for survival of its government at the Centre, there was little room for the saffron party to accommodate Jagan Reddy.
