And that perhaps would be the biggest challenge for Jagan Mohan Reddy.Jagan Mohan Reddy had a bitter parting from the Congress in 2010, a year after the death of his father YS Rajasekhara Reddy. YSR Reddy was in his second term as the chief minister of Andhra Pradesh when he died in a helicopter crash on September 2, 2009. Jagan’s supporters, who were many in number, lobbied hard with the Congress high command for the top post, but Sonia Gandhi did not budge and made K Rosaiah the chief minister. The Congress leadership did not approve of Jagan’s Odarpu Yatra, which was part of his announced plan to meet the families of many people who had sacrificed their lives after his father’s death.That set the stage for his eventual exit from the Congress, which he announced on November 29, 2010 in an open letter to Sonia Gandhi carefully written to ensure there was enough public sympathy for his second phase of political career.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();In the 2014 assembly elections, the YSRCP made an impressive debut and won 67 out of the 175 seats with a vote share of 44.46%, while the Congress could manage only a vote share of 2.8%. The Congress decision to bifurcate the state and create Telangana played a huge role in the party’s declining political fortunes in the state.On November 6, 2017, Jagan embarked on the Praja Sankalpa Yatra and covered 3,648 km in 341 days, crossing 134 assembly constituencies. The Yatra, from YSR Ghat at Idupulapaya to the northeastern tip of Ichchapuram, powered Jagan Mohan Reddy to a historic mandate of 151 seats in the 175-member assembly in the 2019 elections. The Congress’s vote share was reduced to less than 1%.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The Congress, since then, has been making efforts to reclaim its lost political space in the state. It roped in Jagan Reddy’s sister Y S Sharmila as part of the party’s revival plan. Sharmila, who started her political career with her brother Jagan Mohan Reddy eventually drifted towards the Congress and was appointed president of Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee in January 2024.However, both Jagan Mohan Reddy and his sister Y S Sharmila failed to make an impact in the 2024 elections. The 2024 elections saw a dramatic collapse of Jagan’s electoral fortunes, and his party was reduced to only 11 seats. The Congress once again failed to make its presence felt.The 2029 challengeAnd that brings us to the 2029 elections - a do-or-die challenge for both Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress. Jagan’s remark on backing the CEC appointment Bill is his first open “regret” for backing the BJP.But does this “open regret” mean an olive branch for the Congress?Former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha strongly feels that Jagan and Congress should come together, though he admits that this may not be easy.“Politics is the art of the possible and I'm sure Jaganmohan Reddy is aware that Chandrababu Naidu has been an extremely close alliance partner of the Modi government. While the Congress doesn't have a base in Andhra like it used to have once upon a time. The support base of Jaganmohan Reddy is basically the Congress vote which moved away from the traditional Congress to the Congress that Jaganmohan Reddy, branded as the Congress of his father. So, if the merger were to happen, it would, frankly speaking, give them a huge advantage because then both the Central Congress and the Jaganmohan Congress could be on the same page,” Sanjay Jha says.However, he accepts that merger of the two parties could be a difficult process while stitching an alliance may be easier. “Once a political party becomes independent and has power, they don't like to give it up in a hurry. The TMC or the NCP are good examples. In which case it could be an alliance,” Sanjay Jha adds.The third option, according to Sanjay Jha, is for the Congress to resurrect itself on its own strongly in Andhra by capturing both the anti-incumbent votes against Chandrababu Naidu and winning back the loyalist voters of the Congress who had moved over to Jaganmohan Reddy.This is easier said than done. The Congress has a poor track record when it comes to winning back states it has lost. We have seen several states across the country where the Congress has lost its government and eventually its support base but does little to reclaim it.In Andhra Pradesh, Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP are going all out to consolidate their position. Naidu’s call for greater cooperation and coordination among southern states at a recent conference is perhaps an effort to keep his importance and relevance intact. We saw DMK’s MK Stalin make similar moves before he lost power to Vijay’s TVK in the last assembly elections.Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress face an uphill electoral battle in 2029. It will be interesting to see if they can agree to an alliance to take on Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Won't rest till puppet Gyanesh is removed': Cong claims denied permit for mock CEC impeachment; Delhi Police clarifies
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday accused the Centre of denying permission for an event where INDIA bloc parties planned a \"public impeachment\" of Chief
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday accused the Centre of denying permission for an event where INDIA bloc parties planned a "public impeachment" of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, ahead of their November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan.Congress general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal said the government-run Ashoka Hotel had initially allowed the event to be held on its premises but later denied permission following police intervention."The day before yesterday, our people came to construct the infrastructure here and the police stopped them. We don't know what the reason is," Venugopal said."This means it is not the Delhi Police's decision. It is the decision of PM Modi and Amit Shah, and they are protecting their puppet Gyanesh Kumar," he alleged.In a social media post on X, Venugopal also accused the Delhi Police of stopping the party doing the set up for the event at Ramlila Maidan."How many permissions will you deny, Mr. Amit Shah? How many people will you stop? 21 parties of the INDIA bloc had planned a Public Impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar as a curtain raiser to the Nov 1st Mega Rally and March - first at Hotel Ashoka, where permission was denied, and then at Ramleela Maidan, where despite already having all the requisite permissions, Delhi Police stopped us from doing the set up for the event. First they destroy the electoral system, and now they are trying all kinds of tricks to silence those who fight to save our democracy," Venugopal said."Let it be very clear, come what may, we will not rest until Modi-Shah's puppet Gyanesh Kumar is not removed. If they stop us here, we will go to Amit Shah's house, PM Modi's house, and stage a massive dharna there. But we will fight to the finish, and until our mission is accomplished," he added.The proposed event is part of a series of protests by the Congress and other opposition parties demanding Kumar's resignation over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged electoral irregularities.Delhi Police denies chargesMeanwhile, Delhi Police said it had not withdrawn permission for the Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan, adding that there had been no change in the earlier approval.On the proposed mock Parliament event at Ashoka Hotel, police sources said the matter rested with the hotel, as the premises were privately owned."With respect to the Ashoka Hotel mock Parliament, Delhi Police says it depends on the hotel since it's their private premises," Delhi Police sources told news agency ANI.Earlier, Delhi Police had confirmed that a no-objection certificate (NOC) had been issued to the Congress for booking Ramlila Maidan from October 25 to November 3. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said the Congress had approached the police after obtaining a venue availability certificate from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD).Delhi Police's 'terms and conditions'Delhi Police has also laid down a list of "terms and conditions" for the Congress rally on November 1, including installing high-definition CCTV cameras at strategic locations, ensuring the event concludes by 5pm and prohibiting speeches that could disturb communal harmony.In its communication to the Congress, police said there was "no objection" to the rally from a law-and-order perspective, subject to prior permission from the land-owning authority and compliance with the stipulated conditions.The organisers have been asked to install cameras at "all the strategic points including entry/exit gates, stage, all surrounding areas of Ram Lila Ground and sitting enclosures", along with a monitoring system with "atleast 5 screens" and a CCTV control room.They have also been directed to provide "sufficient numbers of water tankers and toilet blocks (separate for female participants)" and deploy volunteers wearing "identical dress or bear common Badges" to ensure the smooth conduct of the rally.The rally must conclude at 5pm on November 1, after which "the dispersal will start and under no circumstance will it be extended". Overnight stays by participants at Ramlila Maidan, either before or after the rally, have also been prohibited.Police has further directed the organisers to ensure that "no speakers would speak anything about caste/creed/colour that can disturb the public harmony, peace and tranquility of the area".If any "instigating/intimidating speech" is made, "the PA system will be switched off immediately", followed by the removal of the speaker from the stage by the organisers.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Israeli firm suspected of using digital ads to track Starlink users in over 100 countries: Report
articles.summary: An Israeli advertising technology company, Discover-Tech, is facing scrutiny over suspicions that its digital advertising activity could be used to track
articles.body: An Israeli advertising technology company, Discover-Tech, is facing scrutiny over suspicions that its digital advertising activity could be used to track people using SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service, according to six people familiar with the findings of cybersecurity researchers.The investigation by TrendAI, a unit of Tokyo-based cybersecurity firm Trend Micro, found that Discover-Tech was among the biggest bidders for advertisements reaching Starlink users. The company reportedly ranked first in bidding for Starlink-related advertising traffic in more than 100 countries, including several where the service is banned or restricted.Researchers believe the unusual pattern could point to an attempt to identify users' locations or monitor them through data collected during online advertising transactions.SpaceX did not respond to requests for comment by news agency Reuters. Discover-Tech and its chief executive also did not respond to requests for comment over the past two weeks.TrendAI published a report on October 15 detailing suspicious activity involving advertisements shown to Starlink users. However, it did not name Discover-Tech, referring instead to an unnamed advertising technology entity under the codename “Shadow-Earth-79”.Six people familiar with the research said the codename referred to Discover-Tech.Asked why it had not publicly identified the company, TrendAI said its approach to attribution was intended to minimise errors and avoid "hype-driven labels" or "unstable actor names that can mislead defenders, distort risk prioritization, and trigger inappropriate response actions."How digital advertising was 'used for surveillance'Online advertising operates through auctions in which advertisers compete for space on websites and apps. During this process, information about internet users can be shared with bidders.Researchers at Canadian cybersecurity watchdog Citizen Lab and New York-based advertising technology firm Confiant named Discover-Tech in separate findings released on the same day as TrendAI's report.Both organisations accused the Israeli company of abusing the advertising bidding system, which can expose information about users to advertisers.By collecting such information across multiple transactions and combining it with other data, an operator could potentially identify people who would otherwise remain anonymous, track their activity across websites and, in some cases, target them with surveillance software.Citizen Lab and Confiant said Discover-Tech's advertisements had appeared within dozens of sensitive networks associated with media organisations, government bodies and technology companies.Following the investigations, Google, Comcast and other companies said they had removed Discover-Tech from their advertising platforms.At least one major US technology company and one international organisation have also launched internal investigations into whether the company's advertisements targeted their employees, according to two people familiar with the matter.The concerns extend beyond ordinary internet users. Identifying the location or activity of people using satellite internet could be particularly sensitive when they include government officials, journalists or personnel operating in conflict zones.Starlink's role in conflict zones raises concernsStarlink provides internet access through satellites operated by SpaceX, allowing people to connect without depending entirely on conventional telecommunications networks within their countries.This can make the service useful in areas where internet access is restricted, communications infrastructure is damaged or conventional networks are unavailable.Ukraine's military has become particularly reliant on Starlink for communications near the front lines and for directing drone strikes. The possibility of identifying or tracking users could therefore raise security concerns in active conflict zones.In May, Israeli newspaper Haaretz and the website Intelligence Online separately reported that Israeli-owned businesses were offering clients ways to identify and track Starlink users. Haaretz reported that the use of digital advertising data appeared to be central to these efforts.TrendAI's report also pointed to unusual advertising patterns across several countries. It described the suspected operator as running "targeting and tracking infrastructure rather than a commercial advertising operation."The entity was identified as the largest buyer of digital advertisements in Syria, Libya, Yemen and South Sudan, and the second-largest in Afghanistan. The report questioned the commercial rationale for such activity, noting that "the demand for legitimate Western advertising in sanctioned or active-conflict states is effectively zero."It also said the entity secured "an implausibly dominant share" of advertising bids in several countries, including Hungary, Israel, Egypt, Azerbaijan and Venezuela.These patterns raised suspicions that the activity might serve a purpose beyond ordinary advertising. However, the findings do not by themselves establish the extent of any surveillance or prove that specific Starlink users were tracked.Why TrendAI did not name Discover-TechAccording to the six people familiar with the research, TrendAI investigators believed Discover-Tech was responsible for the suspicious bidding activity and discussed identifying the company in their report.Five of the sources said the researchers ultimately abandoned that plan after senior executives raised legal concerns.The case highlights a challenge for cybersecurity firms investigating suspected surveillance operations. Publicly naming a company or government as responsible for suspicious activity can carry legal and commercial risks, particularly when the evidence is disputed or difficult to verify independently.Industry experts say some cybersecurity companies avoid making direct accusations because they fear legal action or retaliation.A similar issue arose earlier this year when US cybersecurity company Palo Alto removed explicit references to China from a report on a global cyber-espionage campaign, despite its researchers believing the activity could be attributed to Beijing, Reuters reported.Reuters said the report was toned down amid concerns that directly naming China could create problems for Palo Alto's business operations there. Those operations were already under scrutiny after Beijing directed domestic companies not to use its products.Palo Alto rejected the suggestion that commercial considerations had influenced its decision, saying the lack of attribution was not linked to "procurement regulations in China" and describing any suggestion otherwise as "speculative and false."You use AI every day. articles.title: Greece rallies 3 Arab states against Turkey-Libya sea deal as Crete gas and maritime borders fuel tensions
articles.summary: Greece has secured the backing of Egypt, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates in its dispute with Turkey over a maritime agreement with Libya, as the four
articles.body: Greece has secured the backing of Egypt, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates in its dispute with Turkey over a maritime agreement with Libya, as the four countries warn that the deal threatens regional stability and international law.According to Reuters, the four countries issued a joint statement at the United Nations in New York on Monday, days after Libya’s eastern parliament approved the maritime boundaries agreement originally signed by Turkey and Libya’s Tripoli-based government in 2019.The move has reignited tensions over competing sea claims in the eastern Mediterranean, where Greece and Cyprus say the deal infringes on their maritime rights.Greek foreign minister George Gerapetritis delivered a joint statement at the United Nations on behalf of Greece, Egypt, Bahrain, the UAE, Cyprus and the European Union, declaring the 2019 Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum “null and void”.“The recent decision of the Libyan House of Representatives to approve the 2019 so-called ‘Turkish-Libyan Memorandum of Understanding on the delimitation of maritime jurisdictions in the Mediterranean Sea’ raises serious concerns for regional security and stability,” Gerapetritis said.The joint statement warned that accepting bilateral arrangements that disregard international law “would set a dangerous precedent”, adding that the agreement disregards the maritime rights of coastal states, including the rights of islands under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).The signatories said the Libyan parliament’s approval did not change their position on the agreement’s legal status and called for maritime disputes to be resolved through dialogue and international law.The signatories said the Libyan parliament’s approval did not change their position on the agreement’s legal status and called for maritime disputes to be resolved through dialogue and international law.Turkey has defended the agreement as consistent with international law and the mutual interests of Ankara and Tripoli. Its foreign ministry also welcomed the eastern Libyan parliament’s approval, saying Turkey would continue working with regional partners to promote security, stability and peace in the Mediterranean.What is the Turkey-Libya maritime accord and why is it disputed?Turkey and Libya signed a maritime boundaries agreement on November 27, 2019, seeking to define their respective maritime jurisdiction areas in the eastern Mediterranean.The memorandum was signed in Istanbul by Turkey and Libya’s then internationally recognised Government of National Accord, based in Tripoli. It established a maritime boundary between the two countries’ claimed continental shelves and exclusive economic zones (EEZs), areas that carry rights over natural resources and certain economic activities.The agreement is controversial because its proposed boundary crosses an area where Greece claims maritime rights based on its islands, particularly Crete. Athens argues that Turkey and Libya cannot reach a bilateral arrangement that disregards the maritime entitlements of Greek islands.Turkey, which is not a party to the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), disputes Greece’s interpretation of how islands should affect maritime boundary delimitation.The dispute also has implications for Egypt and Cyprus, which oppose the agreement over concerns that it overlaps with their own maritime claims. Egypt and Greece signed a separate agreement in 2020 establishing an exclusive economic zone in parts of the eastern Mediterranean, a move Ankara opposes.The maritime disagreement has gained importance as countries seek access to potential offshore oil and gas resources. Greece has granted a Chevron-led consortium a licence to explore for hydrocarbons south of Crete, while Athens is pursuing a separate maritime demarcation agreement with Libya.You use AI every day. articles.title: Delhi’s BS6 rule is coming: Is your NCR vehicle on the banned list? Here's how to check
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: If you drive into Delhi from Gurgaon, Noida, Faridabad or Ghaziabad or any other NCR city, your vehicle’s emission standard is about to matter
articles.body: NEW DELHI: If you drive into Delhi from Gurgaon, Noida, Faridabad or Ghaziabad or any other NCR city, your vehicle’s emission standard is about to matter a great deal. From November 1, 2026, Delhi will stop vehicles that fall below BS6 norms and are registered outside the capital from entering.The restriction stays in force until January 31, 2027, as part of the city’s winter pollution control plan.What is the new rule?Applies to vehicles registered outside Delhi that do not meet BS6 standardsEffective November 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027Part of Delhi’s winter action plan, when air quality typically worsensGurugram traffic police have also issued an advisory for commercial goods vehiclesWho will be hit the most?Transport department estimates suggest more than 10 lakh vehicles in neighbouring NCR areas could be affected. Gurgaon and Faridabad together have nearly 2 lakh non-BS6 vehicles, about 70% of them BS3 and BS4, along with around 50,000 commercial vehicles. Noida and Greater Noida have over 4 lakh such vehicles, more than half of them BS4 and mostly petrol cars. Ghaziabad has around 4 lakh.Which vehicles are allowed in?CNG and electric vehicles can still enter Delhi. So can diesel buses and trucks that meet BS6 norms, and buses registered in Delhi. Gurugram traffic police have also warned that BS4 and older commercial goods vehicles, including light, medium and heavy goods vehicles, trucks and buses, will not be allowed in from November 1. This includes vehicles running on All India Tourist Permits.How to check if your car is BS4 or BS6Open the Parivahan Sewa website or app on your phone, and go to “Know Your Vehicle Details” on the VAHAN database. Enter your registration number and complete the verification. Then look for the “Emission Norms” or “Norms” field, which will show whether your vehicle is Bharat Stage IV, Bharat Stage VI or another standard. You can also check your physical or digital Registration Certificate. If the documents are unclear, an authorised dealer or the manufacturer can confirm.How will the rule be enforced?Authorities are tightening checks at Delhi’s borders. Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras and AI-powered cameras will read registration plates and identify vehicles entering the capital. Entry points from Noida, Gurgaon and Ghaziabad are also being strengthened to physically stop non-BS6 vehicles. Around 300 transport department enforcement personnel will be deployed.Why BS6 mattersBharat Stage norms set legal limits on pollutants such as carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons and particulate matter from engines. India has followed BS6 since April 2020, skipping BS5 to speed up pollution control. BS6 vehicles emit far fewer pollutants and need low-sulphur fuel.What’s next?The government plans to bring BS7 norms, aligned with Euro 7, for new cars and SUVs from April 2029, followed by small goods vehicles from April 2030 and heavy-duty vehicles from April 2031.Bottom line: With the deadline just days away, check your vehicle’s norm on VAHAN now to avoid being turned back at the Delhi border.How to check your car’s BS statusVisit the Parivahan Sewa website and open the “Know Your Vehicle Details” service on the VAHAN database.Enter your vehicle’s registration number and complete the verification.Find the “Emission Norms” or “Norms” field in the vehicle record.Read the standard shown, such as Bharat Stage IV or Bharat Stage VI.Check your Registration Certificate (RC), physical or digital, as it may also mention the norm.Ask an authorised dealer or the manufacturer if your documents do not give a clear answer.Know the result: BS6 vehicles can enter Delhi, while BS4 and older vehicles registered outside Delhi will be stopped, unless they run on CNG or electricity.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Óscar Vilda: "La diferencia está en la experiencia que damos al aficionado"
articles.standfirst: El CEO de DAZN España y Portugal analiza junto a Juan Ignacio Gallardo, director de MARCA, los retos del consumo deportivo, la tecnología y la construcción de comunidades de aficionados en la apertura del foro El futuro de las retransmisiones deportivas
articles.summary: El CEO de DAZN España y Portugal analiza junto a Juan Ignacio Gallardo, director de MARCA, los retos del consumo deportivo, la tecnología y la construcción de comunidades de aficionados en la apertura del foro El futuro de las retransmisiones deportivas
articles.body: La transformación del consumo deportivo, el papel de la tecnología y la creciente importancia de la experiencia del aficionado marcaron la conversación que protagonizaron Juan Ignacio Gallardo, director de MARCA, y Óscar Vilda, CEO de DAZN España y Portugal, durante la apertura de la jornada El futuro de las retransmisiones deportivas, organizada por ambas compañías en el Espacio 25 de Unidad Editorial. En una charla en formato entrevista, Vilda repasó la evolución de DAZN desde sus primeros pasos en el mercado español hasta convertirse en uno de los principales actores del sector audiovisual deportivo y la reivindicación de la apuesta de la plataforma por una oferta cada vez más amplia y diversificada. El dirigente recordó que el desembarco de DAZN en España estuvo estrechamente ligado al motor. La adquisición de los derechos de MotoGP en 2019 supuso el primer gran movimiento estratégico de la compañía. "El motor es nuestro origen. Forma parte de nuestro ADN", señaló. Una apuesta que, reconoció, no estuvo exenta de dificultades económicas en sus inicios debido al elevado coste de los derechos, aunque resultó fundamental para construir el crecimiento posterior. Hoy, explicó, España se ha convertido en el segundo mercado de mayor relevancia para el grupo. A MotoGP se sumaron posteriormente la Fórmula 1, los derechos de LaLiga; una oferta que abarca las principales ligas europeas de fútbol, además de competiciones de baloncesto como la NBA y la ACB, sin olvidar disciplinas emergentes en audiencia como el fútbol sala o el fútbol femenino. Más allá de la adquisición de derechos, Vilda puso el foco en el gran reto de las plataformas deportivas: transformar esos contenidos en experiencias capaces de fidelizar al público. "Sin derechos no hay negocio. No tenemos nada que ofrecer", admitió. Sin embargo, considera que la verdadera diferencia ya no está únicamente en poseer los contenidos, sino en cómo se consumen. Ahí es donde DAZN quiere marcar distancia. El ejecutivo insistió en la necesidad de crear un ecosistema que fomente la interacción entre aficionados y genere un auténtico sentimiento de comunidad. "Queremos verlos interactuando unos con otros", aseguró al explicar la estrategia de herramientas sociales que la compañía ha incorporado a sus retransmisiones. Sin ir más lejos, la del último Clásico entre el Barcelona y el Real Madrid: "el segundo evento deportivo más seguido en DAZN de todos los tiempos. Llegamos a tener cuotas de pantalla del 22%", expone Vilda, quien reconoce que el primero fue el Inglaterra - Noruega del Mundial. Vilda destacó además el momento que vive la industria deportiva en España, favorecido por una mayor apertura de clubes, deportistas y competiciones. Puso como ejemplo el reciente Clásico, donde, según explicó, gran parte del atractivo estuvo en el acceso a los protagonistas antes y después del encuentro. "Se está produciendo y eso es imprescindible", afirmó en referencia a unas audiencias cada vez más interesadas en el contenido complementario que rodea al propio evento. En este nuevo escenario, el CEO de DAZN rechazó que la entrada de gigantes globales del entretenimiento en la puja por los derechos deportivos deba interpretarse como una amenaza. Al contrario. Considera que la presencia de nuevos operadores contribuye a reforzar el valor del deporte en la industria audiovisual. "No los veo como una amenaza, sino como una oportunidad", señaló. El objetivo de DAZN, según explicó, pasa por evolucionar desde una plataforma puramente deportiva hacia una gran plataforma de entretenimiento con el deporte como núcleo diferencial. Un activo especialmente valioso porque genera emoción, seguimiento en directo e interacción constante. "Aquí no se puede hacer spoiler", bromeó. La conversación también abordó el desafío de conectar con las nuevas generaciones. Frente a quienes sostienen que los jóvenes se alejan del deporte, Vilda defendió que la pasión sigue intacta, aunque los hábitos de consumo hayan cambiado. Por eso DAZN está apostando por formatos más breves y contenidos adaptados a nuevas formas de descubrimiento, al tiempo que presta una atención creciente al papel de los creadores de contenido digitales. La tecnología aparece como otro de los grandes pilares del proyecto. El directivo destacó las inversiones realizadas para enriquecer las retransmisiones y puso como ejemplo el uso de la inteligencia artificial para ofrecer nuevos puntos de vista en las competiciones de motor. Ese esfuerzo inversor, explicó, también ha sido clave para consolidar el negocio en España y Portugal. La estrategia se ha basado en combinar crecimiento y rentabilidad mediante mayores recursos destinados tanto a contenidos como a innovación tecnológica. Una apuesta que, según defendió, está dando resultados y seguirá guiando los próximos pasos de la compañía. El aficionado, insistió durante toda su intervención, seguirá ocupando el centro de la estrategia. De ahí el impulso a herramientas como Fanzone, donde DAZN ha detectado una implicación especialmente elevada de los usuarios españoles. "El sentido de comunidad que buscamos los españoles es mucho más intenso que en el resto de países", destacó. Esa escucha activa también ha tenido consecuencias directas en la política comercial de la plataforma. Vilda recordó que una de las principales críticas detectadas en los primeros años era el precio de acceso. La respuesta ha sido flexibilizar la oferta para que cada usuario pueda contratar únicamente los contenidos que le interesan. En esa misma línea situó DAZN GO, una iniciativa orientada a ampliar el acceso al deporte y democratizar el consumo deportivo. Una filosofía resumida en una idea que sobrevoló toda la conversación inaugural: en un mercado cada vez más competitivo, la batalla ya no consiste únicamente en ganar derechos, sino en construir experiencias y comunidades capaces de convertir cada retransmisión en algo más que un partido o una carrera.

articles.title: 'We know everything': SC on pleas alleging unilateral decisions by CEC, gives petitioners 10 days to reply
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said that it would examine all aspects of the Election Commission of India's (ECI) decision-making process amid
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said that it would examine all aspects of the Election Commission of India's (ECI) decision-making process amid allegations that key decisions, including those related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were taken without the unanimous consent."We know everything. We will examine," Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said while hearing a batch of petitions challenging the functioning of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the poll panel, Live Law reported.The three-judge bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, adjourned the hearing to November 17.The top court granted the petitioners 10 days to file rejoinders to the ECI’s counter-affidavit, which was submitted on Monday and asserted that the decisions in question were unanimous.The CJI's remark came after senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for leader of opposition on Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, urged the court to direct the ECI to preserve file notings and internal communications related to its decisions.Singhvi argued that the records were crucial to determining whether the decisions concerning the SIR were taken unanimously or unilaterally."This whole issue depends on the decision-making process, consultation, and whether the decision was unanimous or not unanimous. Let file notings, etc be preserved," Singhvi added.The petitions challenge the functioning of Gyanesh Kumar alleged that several ECI decisions, including those related to the SIR, were issued without the concurrence of the other two Election Commissioners.The bench also issued notices to the ECI and other respondents on a fresh petition filed by Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen. The plea alleges that changes were made to Form 6 during the Bihar SIR without the Supreme Court’s approval.Senior advocate and MP Maneka Guruswamy, appearing for Sen, told the court that the poll panel had wrongly claimed that the changes to Form 6 were approved by the top court.The CJI said the court would examine all the issues and asked senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the first petitioner, Rakesh Kumar Singh to file a rejoinder within 10 days to the ECI’s reply affidavit.Earlier on Monday, in its 248-page affidavit, the ECI strongly defended the SIR and rejected allegations that Form 6, the statutory form used for voter registration, had been amended."The attempt to make aspersions against the Election Commission is unfortunate," the affidavit, filed by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu on behalf of the ECI said, PTI reported.The poll panel also maintained that no changes had been made to the statutory Form 6. It said the affidavit itself had been approved for filing through a unanimous decision of all three Election Commissioners.The petitions followed a report published by The Indian Express on September 25, which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over the preceding 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR.According to the report, the two commissioners had objected that the decisions were issued without their knowledge or recommendation.The allegations triggered protests by opposition parties and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which demanded the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The Supreme Court will take up the matter again on November 17, after the petitioners file their rejoinders to the ECI's affidavit.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Pennsylvania man's 2018 vasectomy ended in complications and the loss of a testicle; eight years later, an appeals court has upheld a roughly $9.5 million malpractice verdict against his doctor and practice
articles.summary: A Pennsylvania appeals court has upheld a multi-million-pound medical malpractice judgment against a urologist and his medical practice after a routine
articles.body: A Pennsylvania appeals court has upheld a multi-million-pound medical malpractice judgment against a urologist and his medical practice after a routine vasectomy led to the surgical removal of a patient's testicle. The Superior Court of Pennsylvania upheld the trial court's decision to award damages to Matthew Brennen and his wife, Lisa Brennen, following a jury verdict in Fayette County. The lawsuit arose from a surgical procedure performed in October 2018 by Dr Jason A. Smith, a shareholder at Tri-County Urology Associates, Inc. The ruling ended years of legal disputes over care after the operation, delays in diagnosis, and failures to provide required records before the trial.Surgical procedure and post-operative complicationsMatthew Brennen underwent a routine vasectomy in October 2018 under the care of Dr Smith. According to legal documents filed with the Superior Court of Pennsylvania under docket number 1050 WDA 2025, Mr Brennen suffered extreme pain and serious medical complications soon after the operation. The Brennens later filed a medical malpractice lawsuit against Dr Smith and Tri-County Urology Associates, Inc. The couple claimed that the doctor had failed to carry out a proper examination before the surgery. They argued that this check was important for identifying possible risks and preventing the complications that followed. Medical experts who testified for the couple told the court that Dr Smith had failed to meet the standard of care expected of a specialist. Mr Brennen's continuing complications after surgery and the damage to his tissue eventually forced doctors to perform a gonadectomy, a procedure that surgically removed his left testicle.Fayette County jury verdict and damages breakdownThe case first went before a jury in the Fayette County Court of Common Pleas. The jury found in favour of the Brennens on all claims of medical negligence. The jury awarded Matthew Brennen $8 million in compensation for severe physical pain, emotional distress, embarrassment, and the permanent loss of enjoyment of life. The jury also awarded Lisa Brennen $1 million for loss of consortium, which covers the impact of an injury on a spouse and their marital relationship. Additional costs and penalties brought the total financial award linked to the judgment to approximately $9.5 million. During the trial, the couple's lawyers, Michael Calder and Jennifer Webster, challenged the defence argument that the loss of Mr Brennen's testicle was caused by an unpredictable episode of testicular torsion. This condition occurs when a testicle twists and cuts off its blood supply. The legal team argued that Mr Brennen's age made this explanation unlikely. They pointed instead to failures in the surgery and the doctor's diagnosis.Appellate court review and evidence sanctionsDr Smith and Tri-County Urology Associates appealed to the Superior Court of Pennsylvania. They challenged whether the trial evidence was strong enough to support the verdict and disputed penalties imposed by the trial judge. In an opinion written by Judge McLaughlin, the appeals court rejected the defence arguments and upheld the trial court's decision in full. The court found that there was enough evidence for the jury to conclude that the doctor had failed to meet accepted medical standards. Writing for the panel, Judge McLaughlin stated: "The jury's verdict is supported by substantial evidence that Dr. Smith did not meet the standard of care expected of a urologist during the vasectomy procedure."The appeals court also upheld $60,010 in legal penalties and fees imposed on the defence for failing to follow evidence disclosure rules. The trial court had imposed these penalties because the defence failed to provide complete medical records during the required pre-trial exchange. Judge McLaughlin noted that the defence's failure to provide the full medical records justified the financial penalty. The court highlighted the importance of sharing relevant information during the evidence-gathering stage of a civil lawsuit. The defence can still ask the Pennsylvania Supreme Court to formally review the case.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

Delhi Police had initially withheld permission for the October 30 show, citing specific threat-related intelligence and concerns related to security and law and order.The decision was subsequently reconsidered after the organisers held discussions with police officials and presented plans addressing security, traffic management and crowd control. articles.title: Giorgia Meloni’s email targeted in cyberattack on Italian parliament’s IT systems
articles.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s parliamentary email account was among those targeted in a cyberattack on the computer systems of Italy’s lower
articles.body: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s parliamentary email account was among those targeted in a cyberattack on the computer systems of Italy’s lower house of parliament, with several lawmakers and other institutions also affected, news agency Reuters reported Tuesday.The attack targeted the IT systems of the Chamber of Deputies in recent days, although it was not immediately clear whether Meloni’s account had been accessed. Parliamentary technicians contained the incident, while officials said they had activated protective measures, according to Italian news agency ANSA.“Sources at Palazzo Chigi, the prime minister’s office, told news agency ANSA that the affected account was not the one Meloni uses for government communications.”Officials at the Chamber of Deputies said the incident did not constitute a security emergency, adding that such attacks occur frequently.“All protective measures have been implemented,” ANSA quoted the sources as saying, adding that the response involved cooperation with Italy’s National Cybersecurity Agency.The measures may have included temporarily disabling certain computer system functions, which officials described as standard practice.They also said pressure on IT systems appeared to have intensified in recent days, affecting other national, European and international institutions.The incident comes amid a broader rise in cyberattacks across Italy and Europe in recent years, with governments, infrastructure operators and companies increasingly targeted.
